mcqs.learning_point: Understand force as push or pull
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements correctly describes the nature of a force?

options.A: A force is only present when an object is moving.
options.B: A force is a push or pull that can change the motion or shape of an object.
options.C: A force always makes an object accelerate in the direction of gravity.
options.D: A force is the same as energy and can be stored in an object.

mcqs.answer: A force is a push or pull that can change the motion or shape of an object.
mcqs.explanation: A force is defined as a push or pull that can cause a change in an object's motion (speed or direction) or its shape. Option A is a common misconception; forces can act on stationary objects (e.g., a book resting on a table). Option C confuses force with gravity only, and Option D mixes up force with energy. Therefore, option B correctly captures the definition.

mcqs.question: A child pushes a toy car across the floor and the car starts moving faster. Which effect of the applied force is shown in this situation?

options.A: Change in the shape of the car
options.B: Change in the speed of the car
options.C: Change in the temperature of the floor
options.D: Change in the mass of the car

mcqs.answer: Change in the speed of the car
mcqs.explanation: When the child applies a push, the force causes the car’s speed to increase, demonstrating a change in speed. No deformation of the car (A), temperature change (C), or mass change (D) occurs in this scenario. Hence, option B correctly identifies the effect of the force.

mcqs.learning_point: Recognise changes in speed caused by force
mcqs.question: Two objects, A and B, are released from rest on a smooth horizontal surface. Object A is pulled with a constant force of 5 N, while Object B is pulled with a constant force of 10 N. Which statement correctly compares the changes in speed of the two objects after the same time interval?

options.A: Both objects will have the same speed because the surface is smooth.
options.B: Object A will have a greater speed than Object B because it experiences less force.
options.C: Object B will have a greater speed than Object A because it experiences a larger force.
options.D: Both objects will remain at rest because no friction is present.

mcqs.answer: Object B will have a greater speed than Object A because it experiences a larger force.
mcqs.explanation: According to Newton’s second law (F = ma), a larger net force on the same mass produces a larger acceleration, leading to a greater increase in speed over the same time. Therefore, Object B, pulled with 10 N, accelerates more and attains a higher speed than Object A. Options A and D ignore the effect of force, and B reverses the relationship.

mcqs.learning_point: Recognise changes in direction caused by force
mcqs.question: A stone tied to a string is swung in a horizontal circle. When the string is suddenly cut, the stone moves:

options.A: In a straight line tangent to the circle at the point of release.
options.B: In a curved path continuing the circular motion.
options.C: Back towards the center of the circle.

mcqs.answer: In a straight line tangent to the circle at the point of release.
mcqs.explanation: While the string is intact, the tension provides the centripetal force that continuously changes the stone’s direction, keeping it in circular motion. Once the string is cut, this force disappears, and the stone no longer experiences a force toward the center. According to Newton’s first law, it moves in the direction of its instantaneous velocity at the moment of release – a straight line tangent to the circle. Options B, C, and D describe motions that would require a force that is no longer present.
